images.title: Pentagon = rectangle + triangle
images.purpose: Show a house shaped pentagon cut into one rectangle and one triangle whose areas add.
images.composition: One house shaped pentagon, split by a single horizontal cut, each part's area written inside it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. A pentagon shaped like a house: a rectangle 6 units wide and 4 units tall, filled #0072B2, with a triangle on its top 6 unit side, apex 3 units above that side and centred, filled #E69F00. A dashed #6B7280 line marks the cut between the rectangle and the triangle. Labels: '6 cm' under the bottom edge, '4 cm' beside the right edge of the rectangle, '3 cm' beside a thin dashed vertical from the apex to the cut line (right angle mark at its foot). Inside the rectangle '24 cm²', inside the triangle '9 cm²'. Below the figure 'Total 33 cm²'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Cut the pentagon into shapes you know and add: 24 + 9 = 33 cm².
images.description: Show a house shaped pentagon cut into one rectangle and one triangle whose areas add.
images.context: Concept T5.C1x; one image showing only the main idea.

image_decisions.why: The cut itself is the method; it has to be seen on the shape.
